$comment: THE ENFORCER FOR WD-1 (Spec 122 §1.4 / §1.10; Spec 124 §5 register) — every
`outputs.write_discipline.class` enum value (frozen, x-frozen: true,
step.schema.json definitions.writeDiscipline.properties.class), and every
`sharing.on_contention` enum value (frozen, folded in per Ask A3(ii)), must
carry a disposition row HERE naming whether it has a real, live executor
(`implemented` / `executor_by_runner`), is `banned_for_new` (codegen-capable
or schema-expressible but forbidden for any new descriptor), or is
`retire` (the class was measured-refuted — nothing live ever needed it, or
it is structurally undeclarable). This mirrors grandfathered.json's proven
posture ('adjudication is a reviewed diff, not something a descriptor
grants itself') applied to the ENUM itself rather than to a per-step
guard/retraction exemption.
This file does NOT change step.schema.json's bytes (schema_sha256 stays
byte-identical — verified by generate-template-freeze.mjs --check) and
does NOT remove any enum value (Ask A3 ruling: a `retire`/`banned_for_new`
class stays declarable in the frozen enum; pruning it is a deliberate,
separately-authorized re-freeze, not this WF).
Both directions are enforced by src/tests/write-class-disposition.infra.test.ts:
(0) every row's `disposition` (write_classes AND on_contention) is one of
EXACTLY the four closed-menu values named above — never a free string
(a typo like "implementedd", or an invented fifth value, is RED).
(1) every live enum value (class + on_contention) has a row here, every
`implemented`/`executor_by_runner` row's executor_fn/runners[]
resolve to real exported symbols in scripts/lib/step/write.js or
scripts/lib/step/index.js (grep-verified, not trusted), and no live
descriptor (scripts/*.descriptor.json, scripts/quality/*.descriptor.json)
declares a banned_for_new/retire class OR sharing.on_contention value —
the on_contention half is checked against its OWN registry rows, never
inferred from the class half.
(2)-(4) RED on three shapes: a descriptor declaring a banned class, a
registry missing a live enum row, and an orphan registry row not in
the live enum — so the registry can never silently drift in either
direction.
A row MAY carry an optional `basis` field (e.g. self_skip's "by_construction")
for a nuance that does not change the disposition itself — `basis` is never
part of the closed-menu check, only `disposition` is.
Measured 2026-09-09 @ f3bab336, branch wf2/deep-scrapes-restore-l0, by the
WD-1 WF5 audit (.cursor/wf5_wd1_write_class_audit_active_task.md §1.1/§1.3).
Each `why` below cites the grounded evidence directly, not the plan.

The class is a truthful description of the mechanic (a session TEMP table -> one UPDATE...FROM guarded IS DISTINCT FROM) with no codegen consumer, which is why executor_by_runner is the honest disposition rather than implemented (no write.js branch exists) or banned_for_new (3 live enrich_parcels targets depend on it). The SQL is authored in scripts/lib/compute/enrich-parcels.js (35 client.query( sites, the K3 residual).

verdict_only.why: ZERO mention, and STRUCTURALLY UNDECLARABLE: class exists only under outputs.writes[], and the ASSERT archetype's own frozen x-profile forces outputs to the literal const "none" (step.schema.json:1718) — so NO ASSERT step, including assert_schema (the sole ASSERT representative, Spec 122 §8.2), can ever declare outputs.writes[] at all, let alone a class inside it. assert-schema.descriptor.json already carries a formal deviations[] entry recording exactly this gap FROM §8.2's own class-L assignment. This is not merely unexercised (like H) or refuted-by-measurement (like M) — it is undeclarable BY CONSTRUCTION for the only archetype that was ever assigned it. Closed in commit 3: Spec 122 §1.10 and §8.2's ASSERT archetype row are both amended to state this explicitly.

snapshot_append.why: ZERO mention. x-menu-completeness records the one step Spec 122 §1.4/§8.2 assigned M to (refresh_snapshot, RECORDER archetype) as measured-refuted: "M -> INEXPRESSIBLE" — refresh_snapshot's actual write is a keyed ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE (class A, guarded_upsert/set_source:"compute", executed via executeRecorderUpsert <- runRecorderPhase), not an append-only INSERT into a separate snapshot table. Unlike class L (undeclarable by construction for its whole archetype), M's own archetype (RECORDER) DOES declare outputs freely — the class was simply never the real shape of the one step ever assigned it. Spec 122 §8.2's RECORDER archetype row (currently reading "M") is amended in commit 3 to record this refutation alongside its now-correct class A.

self_skip.why: 9 of 9 converted descriptors declare self_skip; grep -rn on_contention scripts/lib/ scripts/*.js scripts/analysis/ scripts/hooks/ src/ = ZERO readers (only descriptors, schema, and Spec 122 prose). Declared-only, but truthfully so: pipeline.withAdvisoryLock's self-skip terminal is the library's actual, unconditional contention behaviour today, so the field names something real even with no dedicated reader — hence plain 'implemented', with basis:"by_construction" recording the nuance (nothing reads the field to select this) rather than inventing a fifth disposition value. A drift guard (below) is the cheap, non-inventive lock this WF adds (Ask A1).
self_skip.adjudicated_by: WD-1 WF5 audit + Ask A1 recommendation
self_skip.drift_guard: every converted descriptor's sharing.on_contention must equal whichever on_contention key is dispositioned "implemented" in THIS registry (today: self_skip) — derived from the registry, never a hardcoded literal, so the guard cannot silently stay green if a future ruling changes which value is implemented (proven by the infra lock's Ask A1 assertion) — a genuine drift guard, not a new mechanism; rejects the heavier option of inventing an unexecuted runner read of the field.

wait.why: ZERO — no wait/retry/lock-timeout-loop path keyed on this field exists anywhere in scripts/lib/.

fail.why: ZERO — no path raises on contention instead of self-skipping.
